 European drugstore chains roll out Korean-made private-label lines
Spanish supermarket and U.S. beauty retailer join the trend
Japanese and Brazilian drugmakers partner with Korean beauty manufacturers
Exports at three Korean beauty ODM firms surge over three years
 Business | Published 2026.11.15. 14:44:24 | By Kang Dong-heon kaaangs10@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A Products being manufactured at Kolmar Korea's Sejong plant. Photo courtesy of Kolmar Holdings Overseas drugstore chains that once simply sold K-beauty products are increasingly commissioning Korean manufacturers to make their own private-label cosmetics for sale in their home markets. As K-beauty's popularity climbs, foreign retailers are moving to use the "Made in Korea" label as a competitive asset of their own.
 Kruidvat, a major European drugstore chain, launched eight Korean-made private-label products under the name "Kruidvat Korean Skincare" in June, according to beauty industry sources on the 15th. Kruidvat, which operates more than 1,250 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium, had already been selling a range of K-beauty brands including Beauty of Joseon and SKIN1004.
 Mercadona, Spain's largest supermarket chain, released Korean-made PDRN and collagen eye patches in August through its in-house cosmetics brand Deliplus. Last month it added a "K-Skin" line that includes a PDRN serum and a gel cream. Germany's drugstore chain Rossmann also introduced eight skincare products developed and manufactured in Korea in October last year under ISANA, its flagship value-for-money beauty private label. Ulta Beauty, a major U.S. beauty retailer, is selling Korean-made eye patches starting at $8 through its own Ulta Beauty Collection brand.
 Overseas pharmaceutical companies are also tapping Korea's manufacturing expertise to develop high-performance cosmetics. Genecell, the Korean unit of Japanese drug distributor Alfresa Group, signed a contract with Cosmax in September to develop and produce premium cosmetics using stem cell culture supernatant. Cimed, a large Brazilian drugmaker, is investing 80 million reais (about 18.9 billion won) to develop a new skincare brand called Mili with Korea's GDK Cosmetics. Seven products have been developed and produced so far, with plans to expand the lineup to 100 by the end of next year.
 As a result, the customer base for cosmetics original development and manufacturing (ODM) firms has broadened from K-beauty brands expanding abroad to overseas retailers, driving a sharp rise in revenue. Cosmax's export revenue grew to 450.5 billion won last year from 263.6 billion won in 2022. Over the same period, Kolmar Korea's export revenue rose to 90.6 billion won from 41.9 billion won, and Cosmecca Korea's to 73 billion won from 28.9 billion won.
 ODM companies are also expanding production capacity. Cosmecca Korea is investing a total of 200 billion won to build a new production base in Ochang, North Chungcheong Province, while Cosmax is spending 60.5 billion won to expand capacity at its plant in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province.
 "Kolmar Korea will see its capacity expand when its Sejong plant comes online next year, allowing it to absorb at least 30% revenue growth over the next three years," said Kim Myoung-joo, an analyst at Korea Investment & Securities. "Cosmax also takes three to four months for product development and production, shorter than global rivals at five to eight months, giving it an edge in a global cosmetics market where speed to launch matters."
